title: The 2-minute start
summary: Commit to only two minutes. Starting is the hard part; permission to stop after two minutes lowers the barrier.
keywords: begin start stuck cannot start procrastinate tiny two minutes
first_steps: Set a 2-minute timer and only {verb} for that long
Do the very first physical action: {open}

title: Make it ugly on purpose
summary: Perfectionism blocks starts. Aim for a deliberately bad first draft that nobody will see.
keywords: perfect perfectionism draft essay write blank page report assignment
first_steps: Write one messy sentence about {topic}, typos allowed
Type three bullet points about {topic}, even bad ones

title: Body doubling
summary: Working alongside another person, in the room or on a call, makes starting easier for many ADHD brains.
keywords: alone lonely focus company friend call library together
first_steps: Message one friend: "Want to sit on a call while we both work?"
Open a silent study-with-me video and keep it beside your work

title: Shrink the step until it feels silly
summary: If a step still feels heavy, make it smaller. A step that feels almost too easy is the right size.
keywords: too big overwhelm overwhelmed huge heavy massive daunting
first_steps: Just {open}. Nothing else yet
Put your hand on the mouse and look at the {thing} for ten seconds

title: Set up a landing pad
summary: Prepare the environment first: open the file, clear one corner, fill a water bottle. Setup counts as starting.
keywords: setup prepare desk messy environment open file
first_steps: {open} and leave it on screen
Clear just the space in front of your keyboard

title: Pair it with something you enjoy
summary: Bundle the task with a small pleasure such as a favourite playlist, drink or snack, to add dopamine.
keywords: boring dull tedious hate motivation dopamine music
first_steps: Start one favourite song, then {verb} until it ends
Make a drink you like and bring it to the {thing}

title: Start with a question, not an answer
summary: Turn the task into a curious question. Questions are easier to approach than demands.
keywords: research understand confused don't know where to start topic
first_steps: Write one question you have about {topic}
Read only the headings of the {thing}

title: Only the first line
summary: Promise yourself only the title or first line. The rest is optional.
keywords: email write reply message essay title first line
first_steps: Type only the title of the {thing}
Write only the first line of the {thing}, any quality

title: Get it out of your head
summary: Working memory is limited. Brain-dump everything onto paper so your head has room to choose one thing.
keywords: too much everything so many tasks overwhelmed thoughts racing list
first_steps: Write every task in your head on one page, no order needed
Circle the one item that feels smallest

title: A tiny transition ritual
summary: Switching tasks is hard. A short, repeatable ritual such as standing up, a sip of water or three breaths signals a change.
keywords: switch switching distracted tabs scrolling phone change task transition
first_steps: Stand up, take one sip of water, sit back down
Close one tab you don't need right now

title: Read one paragraph
summary: For readings, commit to one paragraph or one page, then decide again.
keywords: read reading chapter textbook paper article pages notes
first_steps: Read only the first paragraph of the {thing}
Look at the pictures or diagrams in the {thing} first

title: Smallest runnable change
summary: For code, aim for one tiny change you can run: a print statement, one function name, one failing test.
keywords: code coding bug program project app function assignment debug
first_steps: Open the project and run it once, just to see where it is
Write the name of one function you'll need, nothing inside it

title: One small zone
summary: Pick one tiny zone, such as one shelf or five items, instead of the whole room.
keywords: clean cleaning room tidy laundry dishes mess
first_steps: Pick up five things and put them where they live
Clear just one corner of the desk

title: Gather before you do
summary: Admin tasks feel heavy because of hidden sub-steps. First just gather what you need into one place.
keywords: form forms bill pay apply application documents admin fees bank
first_steps: Open the {thing} and read only the first heading
Put every document you need for the {thing} in one folder

title: Low-spoon mode
summary: When energy is very low, the kindest step may be a tiny one, or rest. Both count.
keywords: tired exhausted no energy burnout drained sleepy sick
first_steps: Just write the task's name on a sticky note for later
Rest for 5 minutes first, then decide

title: Leave a note for future you
summary: If now isn't the time, write one sentence about where to start next time. This reduces tomorrow's startup cost.
keywords: later tomorrow stop pause not today
first_steps: Write one sentence: "Next time, start by..."
Bookmark the {thing} so it's one click away

title: Gentle focus sprint
summary: A short sprint (5 to 10 minutes) with a built-in break. Short enough to feel doable on a hard day.
first_steps: Set a 5-minute timer and {verb} until it rings
Pick one tiny goal for the next 5 minutes

title: Recall, don't reread
summary: For revision, try recalling one thing from memory before reading. It is active, quick and gives an early win.
keywords: exam test revise revision study quiz memorize
first_steps: Write down one thing you remember about {topic}
Answer one practice question about {topic}, even roughly
